newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday September 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday September 18.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
*After the arrest of Italy's state railway managing director Lorenzo Necci in corruption probe, magistrates do not deny that some government members might be involved in the probe (all).

*Magistrates from Mantua and Venice are investigating Northern League party's secessionist claims and the constitution of a volunteer militia force for the so-called Independent Republic of Padania (all).

*Olivetti's former chairman Carlo De Benedetti and his successor Antonio Tesone have been put under preliminary investigation into the group's financial statements. Chief executive officer Francesco Caio was already under investigation. Olivetti's shares fell to a new record low (all).
*Prime minister Romano Prodi and his Spanish colleague Jose' Maria Aznar have said they both want to join Emu from the start (Corriere).
*Gemina financial holding comes back to profit in first half 1996 results, with a consolidated net profit of 115.1 billion lire (Sole 24 Ore).
*Energy giant Eni reports a 5.5 pct rise in first half 1996 net profits, ahead of a second tranche share offer to its investors due in late October (Sole).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
